transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jonah Reed (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Aventis CTO), Lena Ortiz (Aventis ML Eng), Marta Ruiz (Aventis Infra), Samir Patel (Aventis PM)

Summary:
Quick sync on latest POC bench numbers comparing Redwood POC vs their legacy provider (LegacyCloudAI). Discussed latency P50/P95, throughput at target QPS, routing fallbacks, and next steps: deeper 24h load run, share raw logs, and security handoff. Some background noise and a couple of inaudible sections.

Topics:
- P51/P95 differences (note: P51 mentioned once due to transcription)
- Cold start vs steady-state latency
- Batching and quantization tradeoffs
- Routing to fallback model under load
- Dedicated slot request for longer run

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is our weekly POC bench sync with Aventis, we'll go through the numbers, then Priya will call out the tuning changes we made this sprint, and then open up for infra questions. Carlos, Samir — you on video?
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: yeah hi, can you hear me? a little echo on my side but yeah we're good.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: hi all, ready.
[00:18] Priya Shah: cool, i'll kick off with the headline numbers. quick context: we ran three workload profiles mirroring the baseline traces Aventis sent last week: short responses (<=64 tokens), mid (65-256), and long (257-1024). the Redwood runs used optimized kernel selection + prefix cache enabled.
[00:35] Priya Shah: results, short responses: P50 18ms, P95 64ms, throughput 380 qps sustained per 4-GPU pod. baseline (LegacyCloudAI) reported P50 32ms, P95 120ms, throughput ~220 qps on their equivalent machine type.
[00:55] Marta Ruiz: wait those numbers for Redwood — are they with KV cache warm?
[00:58] Priya Shah: yes warm K-V cash — sorry K-V cash in the transcript — warm KV cache. for steady-state; cold starts are slightly higher, P95 around 90ms for short after one-off cold.
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: interesting, that's a pretty solid improvement on P95 but throughput real world matters to us because of spikes.
[01:18] Ethan Park: totally. on throughput we saw 12% variance across 30m window for the short workload when we let cluster autoscale off; with our suggested dedicated slot and auto-burst enabled we can keep it much flatter.
[01:32] Samir Patel: can you quantify burst costs? like the incremental cost when we go from reserved to burst?
[01:36] Priya Shah: rough numbers: reserved dedicated slot is X — ok i'll avoid dollar figures on the call, but we sent a cost sheet. the key levers are batching (we tuned from batch size 8 to 16 for short tokens) and quantization profile (int8 vs fp16) — the int8 path reduced token inference time by ~9% but introduced slight quality diffs on their long summaries.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: what about latency tails for mid-length? the mid workload P95 seems close between providers last sprint.
[02:06] Priya Shah: mid: Redwood P50 34ms, P95 140ms; baseline P50 50ms, P95 165ms. so we still beat them but margin less. mid-length sequences trigger attention kernels that are less optimized in baseline; we applied kernel tiling and got better memory locality which helped.
[02:26] Jonah Reed: note — some of the baseline numbers were reported by Aventis instrumentation which might include network hops to their infra; our infra numbers are measured at the pod egress which can make them look slightly better. would be great to replay their full trace to ensure apples-to-apples.
[02:40] Carlos Mendes: yes we can share a sanitized trace — we'll scrub PII. we'll aim to get that by next friday.
[02:47] Priya Shah: perfect.
[02:48] [02:48] Unidentified Speaker: [inaudible]..
[02:52] Ethan Park: going back to throughput — for long responses the baseline has higher CPU cold overhead, Redwood long response throughput on a 4-GPU pod was ~95 qps sustained vs baseline 65 qps. but the long P95 on our int8 path moved from 720ms to 680ms so not huge.
[03:18] Marta Ruiz: are those numbers inclusive of model quantization and packing? we saw some artefacts with int8 on some prompt types.
[03:25] Priya Shah: we profile a few prompt archetypes, and yes int8 shows some hallucination increase for very long context completion; we suggested mixed-precision for long and int8 for short.
[03:34] Samir Patel: what's the plan for routing? if we keep two model variants (int8 and fp16) will Redwood route based on latency SLA?
[03:40] Priya Shah: yes — we can route by policy: latency SLO triggers fp16 path, cost preference triggers int8, and we can do canary at per-route level. the runtime supports automatic fallback to fp16 if int8 quality degrades on a given prompt set.
[03:52] Carlos Mendes: okay good. on the friday run we saw a couple of spikes that coincided with DB maintenance, so one ask — can Redwood run a 24h load run that includes a synthetic spike to mimic our traffic burst pattern?
[04:03] Priya Shah: yes we can. we'll need a representative traffic sample — we requested that — and a dedicated slot for 24h would ensure consistency.
[04:10] Ethan Park: i'll put up a dedicated slot request in the portal, Priya will run the load test.
[04:14] Priya Shah: flagged. i also want to call out we changed the batching window from 20ms to 10ms which reduced average latency at the cost of slightly lower batching efficiency — net win for p95.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: can you share the raw logs? especially the per-token timing and KV cache hit rates. that's what our team uses to reconcile.
[04:33] Priya Shah: yes we'll share per-route latency CSV and the raw bench logs — they're attached in the shared drive after the call.
[04:39] Samir Patel: any comments on SLO and SLAs — we may need enterprise terms. is Redwood able to commit to per-route latency SLOs during Dedicated?
[04:47] Jonah Reed: yes for dedicated we have SLA-backed targets; we'll need to scope the commit (QPS per slot and model family) — CSM will coordinate with legal for enterprise terms.
[04:56] Carlos Mendes: security-wise we need SOC2 report and SSO integration notes; our security team will want to validate KMS flow for keys.
[05:04] Ethan Park: we will push the SOC2 and SSO doc links to you after this. jonah will handle the security handoff.
[05:09] Jonah Reed: noted, i'll share the security packet.
[05:12] [05:12] Unidentified Speaker: [crosstalk]
[05:14] Priya Shah: quick deeper detail on the spike behavior: during synthetic 2x burst our routing fallback triggered and a small percent of requests hit the fallback fp16 variant which kept latency within SLOs but increased cost by ~8%. that's expected and we can tune thresholds.
[05:30] Marta Ruiz: is there a way to pre-warm KV cache across model restarts? we had issues when redeploying.
[05:36] Priya Shah: yes there is a pre-warm API; we can also persist certain prefixes on startup. it's part of the private deployment options as well where you keep warm state across instances.
[05:46] Lena Ortiz: ok that would help. also curious about observability — can you provide token-level cost breakdown per route?
[05:53] Ethan Park: yes the console gives token and model-level cost and latency breakdowns — we can export CSVs.
[05:58] Samir Patel: a question about the baseline numbers — they included their outbound network time, could that be inflating their P95?
[06:03] Priya Shah: likely; we observed artifacts where baseline's reported P95 spiked during cross-region egress. we recommend running both traces through the same measurement pipeline.
[06:13] Carlos Mendes: we'll do that.
[06:15] [06:15] Short pause / typing
[06:20] Priya Shah: ok next steps: 1) Aventis to share anonymized 30m trace; 2) Redwood runs 24h dedicated slot test with synthetic spikes; 3) Redwood shares raw logs, per-token CSV, and security docs; 4) follow-on pricing note if dedicated reserved capacity is requested.
[06:36] Ethan Park: let's call out timeline: we'll try to get the 24h run scheduled early next week, deliver logs by EOD the day it completes. action items in the notes.
[06:47] Carlos Mendes: sounds good. question — is there a quick win we can flip in prod to improve P95 now while we wait for the longer run?
[06:55] Priya Shah: yes two quick wins: reduce batching window to 10ms (we rolled already on POC), and enable warm KV cache pre-warm hook at deploy. both low risk.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: can we see sample prompt-level diffs when moving int8 to mixed-precision? we'd like to validate hallucination delta.
[07:12] Priya Shah: we'll include a small eval set and diff report with the logs.
[07:16] Samir Patel: okay. any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:19] Ethan Park: none. ready to run when we get the trace and slot confirmation.
[07:23] Jonah Reed: i'll set up the security packet send and include the on-call details.
[07:28] Carlos Mendes: thanks, appreciate the quick turn.
[07:30] Ethan Park: thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

Meeting end.
